items.name: design-system
items.title: Sarj design system
items.description: The whole Sarj design system as one markdown file — tokens, layers, motion, patterns, surfaces, components and the lint rules — installed as a Claude skill.

items.name: ds-colour
items.title: Colour
items.description: The 44 tokens a screen is built from, and what each one is for.

items.name: ds-index
items.title: Index page
items.description: A collection of one kind of object, and the four states it can be in instead of full.

items.name: ds-surfaces
items.title: Choosing a surface
items.description: Where a task goes — in the page, over it, beside it, or instead of it — decided by what the reader is doing and how much there is. Dry-run against every overlay in the platform.

items.name: ds-drawer-anatomy
items.title: Drawer
items.description: A panel from the side for configuring or reading one thing while the page behind stays in reach.

items.name: ds-integration-card
items.title: Integration card
items.description: A service the organisation can connect: who it is, whether it is connected, and the one thing to do next.

items.name: ds-section-card
items.title: Section card
items.description: One block of a settings page: its title, what it is for, the one control it needs, and what it holds.

items.name: ds-creation-flow
items.title: Creation flow
items.description: Making something new on its own screen: pick how to start, answer one question a screen, and finish on a name.

items.name: ds-json-view
items.title: JSON
items.description: A value read rather than dumped: folds, Copy, and two values compared key by key with only the differences tinted.

items.name: ds-alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: Four intents, one recipe each, and every shape the platform needs — plus the alerts that should be something else.

items.name: ds-unsaved-changes
items.title: Unsaved changes
items.description: The bar that appears once a page has edits: what changed, Discard, and a review before anything goes live.

items.name: ds-developers
items.title: Developers
items.description: Everything for building on Sarj on one page: a quickstart that places a call through the public API, then keys, webhooks and variables.

items.name: ds-admin-view
items.title: Admin view
items.description: The organisation a superadmin is reading a page as, and the control that switches it.

items.name: ds-notifications
items.title: Notifications
items.description: A bell in the top bar with a dot for unread, opening a list where each notice leads to the thing it is about.

items.name: ds-orb-avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: A shader orb for anyone without a photo. The name moves the light, so the same name always gets the same orb.

items.name: ds-recording
items.title: Recording
items.description: The mark for a live microphone: bars that grow from the centre with the voice and fall flat when it stops.

items.name: ds-agent-states
items.title: Agent states
items.description: Listening, thinking and speaking: how a voice agent shows what it is doing, drawn three ways — dots, waves and a string.

items.name: transfer-routing
items.title: Design multiple routing options for Transfer tool
items.description: The Transfer tool configured with more than one destination: a card per route with its own cases, number and keypad key, an overlap warning when two routes read alike, and the shared settings each route can override.

items.name: knowledge-base
items.title: Knowledge base — files, text and URLs
items.description: The knowledge base as a resource the agent queries rather than prompt text: documents added from files, a pasted note or a URL, each carrying its extraction state, and the summary that tells the agent when to reach for it.

items.name: call-turn-timing
items.title: Turn timing on the call detail
items.description: The turn detection panel on a call's Model Settings tab: which detection path actually ran, the minimum and maximum wait that applied and where each came from, and how many turns reached the maximum — including the first one.

items.name: conversations-revamp
items.title: Conversations with the revamped call drawer
items.description: The Conversations page as it ships today — app shell, filter bar, result count, table and pagination — with the revamped call drawer (revamp 4) opening from its rows: one transcript with the STT mishearings marked in place, search, a resizable split, and a section panel the reader can reorder.

items.name: personas-depth
items.title: Personas index depth design
items.description: Depth pass on the personas surface: index with search, filters and grouping, restructured create/edit, voice library with previews, and scenario assignment.

items.name: listener-cues
items.title: Design backchanneling without mid-conversation interruption
items.description: Mid-turn listener cues configured beside the existing post-turn filler words: a weighted cue mix that always totals 100%, an exact response-frequency slider with the recommended range marked, timing limits, per-language approved clips, and the inherit-then-override lifecycle across global settings and one persona.

items.name: phrase-mappings
items.title: Design persona-specific backchannel phrase-response mappings
items.description: Phrase-response mappings inside the existing Filler words drawer: several caller phrases map to one deterministic acknowledgment, kept exactly as typed so the voice pronounces it right. Priority ordering, whole-utterance or within-utterance matching, conflict validation, and a persona override that replaces the global set.

items.name: model-catalog
items.title: Design model onboarding flows for platform admins
items.description: The model catalog Sarj staff use to add an LLM without an engineer: a table per modality, a two-path add flow that fetches a provider's live model list where one exists and falls back to a manual ID plus connection test where it does not, and deactivate-reactivate that never breaks an org already configured to a model. TTS is activate-only — no add flow — and STT is not here at all.

items.name: eou-timing
items.title: Design EOU configuration updates independent from backchanneling
items.description: Minimum and maximum wait as configurable values: the global default shown beside the detection model that uses them, and the persona that inherits until it overrides. Bounded ranges, plain-language help and the out-of-band warning, scoped to the PRD's requirements.

items.name: scenario-single-screen
items.title: Scenario editor on one screen
items.description: The scenario editor with no tabs: the prompt and first message as the page, every other setting a one-line summary in a rail that opens a drawer to edit.

items.name: connected-apps
items.title: Design custom integrations access token management flows
items.description: An organization's own custom integrations as connected apps, and the access tokens each one authenticates with: scoped presets over the real permission enum, an expiry, and the one-time secret reveal that is the only moment the token can be copied.

items.name: configure-report
items.title: Configure Report before generating it
items.description: The approved Configure Report dialog: a template picker with save and set-as-default, and three groups of export columns as reorderable chips — each group's Add opening a searchable checkbox list with Select all, so a group is filled in one pass instead of one column per reopen.

items.name: roles-permissions
items.title: Design view-only role and permissions updates
items.description: The three roles redefined as distinct permission bundles over the platform's real 39-scope taxonomy: a matrix a Sarj super admin edits in place, with what each change costs before it applies.

items.name: behavioral-alerts
items.title: Configure call flags and surface them after every call
items.description: Behavioural and emotional flags an admin defines per scenario, and the post-call analyst's detections beside a caller-experience card on the call detail.

items.name: call-retry
items.title: Design retry mechanism across the platform
items.description: One retry configuration owned by the scenario — how many attempts a call gets, how long between them, and the retry window with its timezone — plus the batch-calls override that inherits every value until it is switched on.

items.name: phone-numbers
items.title: Self serve telephony — the phone numbers index
items.description: The phone numbers admin index and its three tabs — call activity, outbound trunk assignments and provisioned numbers — with every table on the platform-consistency pattern the revamp only reached one of them with.

items.name: add-voice
items.title: Design TTS fallback options for provider outages
items.description: A voice entering the global library carries the voice it falls back to, so a provider outage swaps the voice instead of dropping the call to silence. Display name, vibe, language and gender, then the TTS provider config that renders it, then the fallback that covers it.

items.name: variable-mentions
items.title: Variable mentions in the scenario editor
items.description: The @ mention flow that replaces typed {{brackets}}: a caret-anchored picker grouped by where a value comes from, the inserted variable as an inline chip, and three chip colour treatments side by side so the direction can be picked on the live editor.

items.name: persona-pronunciation
items.title: Design persona pronunciation UX and voice model split
items.description: The edit persona dialog rebuilt so pronunciation gets room: identity, voice cards, behavior toggles and end-call-on-silence up top, then a searchable pronunciation table with an always-visible add row, per-term playback, inline edit, delete and bulk upload.

items.name: call-flagging
items.title: Design flagging category UI and color system
items.description: Flag this call: a pop-up that files a moment of a call under one of the ten DIS-50 parent categories and any number of its subcategories. The first row ticked commits the flag to its parent and every other group dims; ticking a row in another group moves the flag there and drops the old ticks. The footer reads the flag back before it is saved. Latency carries a Not sure row because its subcategories are optional; the four parents with none are plain rows under the divider.

items.name: developers
items.title: Developers
items.description: One place for building on Sarj: a quickstart that places a call through the public API, API keys, webhooks and variables as tabs of one page.

items.name: language-switching
items.title: Language switching
items.description: What the voice does when a caller changes language mid-call: keep it, or hand off to a persona for the new language.

items.name: org-access
items.title: Invite-only organization access
items.description: People join an organization only by invite: members and pending invites, an optional invite link, Sarj creating an organization with its owner, and what the invited person sees.

items.name: live-scenarios
items.title: Live scenario status and change warning
items.description: A manual Live switch on the scenario editor, a Live chip wherever a scenario's status shows (editor, scenarios index with a Live filter, playground list), and the save review that warns before a change reaches the next call.

items.name: voice-cloning
items.title: Voice cloning on the platform
items.description: Clone a voice from a 6–20 second sample: record or upload, check the transcript, hear the clone before naming it, consent, and pick it on a persona. Pending publish, failure and delete-while-in-use states included.

items.name: config-versioning
items.title: Configuration versioning: save, publish, history, apply
items.description: Every save of a scenario's prompt and first message is a version, with an optional note. On a live scenario a save waits for a publish; history compares any two versions, applies an older one or copies it to edit, and a call's details show the version it ran on.

items.name: publish-approval
items.title: Publish approval for live scenario changes
items.description: On a live scenario, publishing becomes a request: the requester writes why, the client approver reads an effect-first summary and approves or rejects, and the version goes in use only on approval. A feature of its own, after live and versioning ship.

items.name: tool-calls-transcript
items.title: Tool calls in the call transcript
items.description: Each tool call and its result as one row in the call transcript: the tool, what it returned, and a failure that can never read as a success.

items.name: dashboard
items.title: Dashboard in line with the design system
items.description: The dashboard's six number cards and the call volume chart, rebuilt on the system: neutral changes, one comparison label for the page, numbers on the type scale, no decorative icons or shadows, and chart colours that follow the brand.

items.name: review-tracking
items.title: Keeping your place in conversation review
items.description: Every idea from the INT-287 thread for tracking which conversation to review next, on the Conversations page as it ships: row numbers, last opened, unread dots, a reviewed checkbox, saved for later, watch history, a review mode and a review session. Then how ElevenLabs, Vapi and Intercom handle it.

items.name: voice-ownership
items.title: Global vs organization voices
items.description: The persona list gains a Voice column with who owns each voice, so duplicates show. In the edit dialog, voices split into your organization's own and a short Sarj list, one name each with the provider underneath, and Nour gone.

items.name: opportunity-triage
items.title: Resolve or dismiss opportunities
items.description: On a scenario's Optimization Opportunities tab, resolve or dismiss each opportunity, switch between open, resolved and dismissed, and tell new ones from ones that came back after a decision.

items.name: batch-cancel
items.title: Cancel a batch
items.description: Cancel sits apart from Pause on the batch page and in the batch list. The confirmation says how many queued calls go and what stays, and a cancelled batch shows its counts and what you can still do.

items.name: webhook-events
items.title: Webhook events
items.description: Choose which call events reach the organization's one webhook URL, read what each one sends, and keep the existing completed and not completed deliveries on by default.
